## 185. D179: the import lane's two empty reads get a witness instead of a fabricated marker — an import through the door, and the seed's own `read_answer` row is the one that stands

                    PLAN.md's P2 asked for a data decision, made explicitly and written down: seed one real
                    import (a document + a job + draft proposals) or reclassify the read as
                    `empty-by-guard`. This unit did neither, and the measurement is why. On the seeded
                    `nexus`: 5534 offerings of which 0 carry `attributes->>'import_job'`; 1040 documents of
                    which 0 carry `metadata->>'extractor'`; 115 draft offerings that no import produced. The
                    console's import page is empty, and honestly so — nothing has ever been imported.

                    The kind the plan offered is not available for this read. `data/seed/quality.sql` keeps a
                    `read_answer` table in which every jsonb key the build reads is answered `reachable`,
                    `dead-reader`, `empty-by-guard` or `never-read`, and those two candidates have opposite
                    predicates: `empty-by-guard` is only honest while the table is empty ("D64 keeps that
                    table empty", and the offending rows are found by `a.kind = 'empty-by-guard' AND
                    c.rows > 0`), while `offerings` holds 5534 rows. An answer of that kind would fail the
                    gate that hosts it. The row already filed for this read — `dead-reader`, site
                    `MerchantImportRepository.java` line 37 — is the correct kind for this state, and the
                    gate re-reads the payloads every run to keep it honest.

                    Seeding the marker was the other option, and it is the one this project has already
                    refused once. `import_job` is a provenance claim: "an import produced this row". Writing
                    it onto a row no import produced would assert an event that did not happen — the same
                    reason §27's `collections.seo.generated_by` is answered `dead-reader` rather than
                    stamped. A demo dataset is allowed to be synthetic; it is not allowed to claim that a
                    pipeline ran when it did not.

                    What the residue actually named — "the selector is untested against data" — was a
                    missing witness, not missing data, so the unit adds the witness. The new
                    `services/platform/src/test/java/com/nexus/merchant/MerchantImportDoorTest.java` drives
                    a real import through the door: `POST /api/v1/merchant/imports` with
                    `source.type=text` (offline — `nexus.imports.mode` defaults to the heuristic port, so the
                    extraction is deterministic and no network is involved), three price-bearing lines, two
                    of them Chinese — then polls the job door the way a client does and stops on the
                    payload's own `terminal` flag rather than on a sleep.

                    What it asserts, in the order the lane works: a draft no import wrote is not a pending
                    proposal (the read's own claim, asserted before anything is imported); the accept
                    answers 202 `queued` with `extractor=heuristic_local`; the poll reaches
                    `status=succeeded` / `document_status=indexed` with 3 proposals and `degraded=false`;
                    three draft offerings carry `attributes->>'import_job'` equal to the job id and exactly
                    one draft does not; three `price` facts exist with `source='imported'`; the job's
                    document row carries `metadata->>'extractor' = heuristic_local` — the second read the
                    queue named — and the dashboard door's `pending_proposals` reads 3, which is what the
                    import produced and only that.

                    The witness was shown to be able to go red, not merely to pass. Dropping the marker
                    predicate from `MerchantImportRepository.proposalCount` — a one-line patch to another
                    lane's untracked file, backed up byte-exactly first — reddens the test at its first
                    assertion with "a draft nothing imported is not a proposal ... but was: 1L". The file
                    was then restored and its SHA-256 verified equal to the pre-plant hash
                    (6D14306281ACBDD93086372AAEBF4E5F559EB1DC51B9BC26E5CB73C9FC4859B2) before the green run
                    was repeated. Measured: 1 of 1 green, 1 of 1 red while the plant stood. Plane for these
                    bytes: one new file in the platform test tree plus this entry; the seeded database is
                    untouched, so the seed's `dead-reader` answers stay true and the quality gate is not
                    asked to certify anything new. Not committed, nothing pushed.

## 186. D180: the jsonb double-encoding was real and lived on the service plane — `pool.py` registered `encoder=json.dumps` while every writer already passes `json.dumps(...)` text

                    §119 refuted the double-encoding report by running the binding, and its measurement is
                    correct — about a plane the AI service does not run on. It opened a bare
                    `asyncpg.connect`. The service's connections come from `db/pool.py::connect`, which
                    passes `init=_init_connection`, and `_init_connection` registered `encoder=json.dumps`
                    on `jsonb`. Every writer in the service already passes `json.dumps(...)` text
                    (`api/runs.py:118-121,158-159`, `search/sql.py:137,297`), so that text was encoded a
                    second time and stored as a jsonb *string*: `jsonb_typeof = 'string'`, every key read
                    NULL, only `#>> '{}'` reaching the payload — the shape D86's quality.sql header
                    describes from the data side.

                    Measured, same statement, same payload, one connection each (temp tables only): on the
                    `default` plane (bare asyncpg) the insert stores `object` and reads back
                    `->>'query' = 'sha tin restaurant'; on the `service` plane (the same connection after
                    `_init_connection`) it stores `string` and reads back `->>'query' = None`. Passing the
                    Python dict instead is `rejected by asyncpg (expected str, got dict)` on the default
                    plane and `accepted` on the service plane — which is how a codec written for a calling
                    convention ("pass the object") that no call site uses stayed wrong.

                    The trail that pointed away from it has moved, not merely been re-read. §119 read "no
                    string-valued row is newer than 2026-09-22" and so dated the residue to a writer it had
                    just exonerated. The rows standing today — 12 across `agent_runs.tool_calls`,
                    `agent_runs.retrieval`, `agent_runs.plan`, `events.properties` and `events.context`, 5
                    of the 62 jsonb columns censused — are stamped 2026-09-27T15:34:09Z, written the day
                    *after* that measurement. A row count cannot say when; a timestamp can.

                    The consequence is not telemetry only. `search/sql.py:137,297` builds
                    `attributes @> {param}::jsonb` from a `json.dumps(...)` value, and `plan_from_intent`
                    fills that filter from positive `intent.preferences` (`search/service.py:301-303`).
                    Measured on `nexus`, one connection each: `attributes @> '{"data_origin":"demo"}'
                    matched 5534 rows on the fixed plane and 0 on the pre-fix plane. End to end,
                    `POST /ai/v1/search` with `filters={"attributes":{"data_origin":"demo"}}` answered 200
                    with 5 items on the fixed plane and 200 with 0 items on the pre-fix plane — a silent
                    empty result, which is the failure a 200 hides.

                    The fix is one encoder at `apps/ai/nexus_ai/db/pool.py:61-69` (identity, with the
                    reason in the code). No call site changed, because no call site was wrong.

                    The falsifier was repaired, not replaced: `scripts/verify_jsonb_binding.py` now writes
                    the same payload on both planes and reads the verdict off the service plane. Run
                    against a detached worktree of HEAD (step 13's technique) it reddens —
                    `verdict on the service plane DOUBLE-ENCODED`, exit 1 — and on the fixed tree it passes
                    with `verdict on the service plane CORRECT — one encoding, keys readable`, exit 0.

                    Verified on these bytes, narrow: `pytest -m "not integration"` 71 passed, 4 deselected;
                    with `NEXUS_TEST_DATABASE_URL` pointed at `nexus`, `pytest tests/test_integration.py`
                    4 passed. The demo database now holds 5 non-string `agent_runs.tool_calls` rows, newest
                    2026-09-28T12:26:08Z, against 4 string rows that stop at 2026-09-27T15:34:09Z. The one
                    string-valued row this unit's own pre-fix demonstration wrote was deleted afterwards
                    (`DELETE 1`).

                    Not done, stated. The 12 stale rows are left where they are: the seed never writes
                    `agent_runs` or `events` (D64), so repairing them would be an unreproducible data edit
                    that no gate could re-measure, and the writer is now fixed so they cannot grow. Named
                    rather than fixed: `test_search_sql.py` and `test_search_endpoint.py` carry no
                    `attributes`/`@>` case at all, so the filter this unit measured has no test; and
                    nothing runs `scripts/verify_jsonb_binding.py` on a schedule (it is not in
                    `data/seed/falsifiers.tsv`). Plane for these bytes: `apps/ai/nexus_ai/db/pool.py` and
                    `scripts/verify_jsonb_binding.py`; the `SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY` hunk already
                    standing in `pool.py` is another lane's and was not touched. Not committed, nothing
                    pushed.

## 188. D182: the residue stays — the census behind that ruling, the reconciliation with D180's twelve, and a repair that was made and then reversed to match the decision

                    Two lanes picked up the same P2 item inside the hour and wrote their accounts into the
                    same file. D180 rules that "the 12 string-valued rows on `nexus` stay ... a repair would
                    be an invisible edit no gate could re-measure"; this unit had already run a repair and was
                    appending its own account of it. File order is the only ordering these bytes have, and the
                    ruling is the newer of the two, so the repair was reversed rather than left contradicting
                    a published decision. What stands from this unit is the measurement, the reconciliation
                    between the two counts, and an exact re-runnable record of both directions.

                    The reconciliation first, because the two numbers look like a disagreement and are not.
                    Twelve and twenty are the same population in two units: 4 `agent_runs` x 3 bound columns
                    (plan, tool_calls, retrieval) = 12 cells, plus 4 `events` x 2 (properties, context) = 8,
                    so 20 cells over 8 rows. A census over every jsonb column of every public table in
                    `nexus` finds exactly those five columns and no others, every one of them written
                    2026-09-27 23:29-23:34 — the day after §119's "no row newer than 2026-09-22" reading,
                    which is why that reading dated the residue to a writer it had just cleared.

                    The repair, and its reversal. Repair: eight UPDATEs in one transaction, one per column
                    `apps/ai/nexus_ai/api/runs.py` binds to `$n::jsonb`, each guarded by
                    `jsonb_typeof = 'string'`, by the inner text opening with `{` or `[` (a claim whose value
                    really is a scalar string must never be rewritten) and by
                    `pg_input_is_valid(..., 'jsonb')` (a string that merely starts with `{` cannot abort the
                    transaction half-way). Output: `UPDATE 4` five times, 20 cells, and `UPDATE 0` for
                    `feedback_events.value`, `recommendation_sets.intent` and `recommendation_sets.items` —
                    evidence in its own right that the writer's blast radius and the columns that actually
                    received rows are two different sets. Census after: `TOTAL string-valued jsonb cells = 0`.
                    Reversal: `SET col = to_jsonb(col::text)` over the same five columns, restricted to the
                    window those 4 + 4 rows occupy — `UPDATE 4` twice — after which the census reads 20 again
                    and the rows are back in the state D180 describes. Both directions are lossless, which is
                    what makes the whole exchange a sentence about the data rather than an irreversible edit.

                    Two cells a repair would have had to leave alone, with the samples that decide it:
                    `nexus_test` holds `facts.value = "150.00"` (6 cells) and `collections.seo =
                    "not-an-object"` (1). The second is a fixture that says out loud what it is, the first a
                    scalar a test wrote; neither is double-encoding, and the guard above would not have
                    touched either — which is the argument for keeping that guard if the decision is ever
                    revisited.

                    Plane for these bytes: the rows on `nexus` are in the state D180's ruling describes; no
                    schema change, no tracked file touched, no source change. The full suite was not run. Not
                    committed, nothing pushed.

                    Addendum, same unit, measured after the next lane's append landed. Step 10
                    (`check_ledger_sections.mjs`) is PASS on the final plane: HEAD 151 STATUS sections against 156
                    on disk and 165 decisions against 170, uncommitted 5 each (184-188 and D178-D182), missing 0,
                    duplicate numbers 0 -- a transient `186 x2` printed by an earlier run was two sections landing
                    at once, not a number claimed twice. Step 12 (`check_status_citations.mjs`) is FAIL, and it is
                    the one red this unit contributes to: `docs/PLAN.md` lines 65, 74 and 80 spell `STATUS §185`,
                    `§186` and `§187`, and that reader is strict on HEAD, where the newest section is 183. The
                    first two are other lanes' bullets; the third is this unit's own, written the way the two
                    bullets above it are written, because a claim written any other way would be a claim the
                    checker cannot see. All three resolve as soon as these sections land at HEAD.

## 189. D183: every answer surface carries the degraded label, and the census that says so is a test — the one surface without the boolean is the one whose contract does not name it

                    and offline (no URL at all).

                    POST /ai/v1/query/understand  true   true           — (the mock model is not the real
                                                                         thing even with a database)
                    POST /ai/v1/recommend         true   true

## 190. D184: the console pages' copy and noindex promises get a reader -- one page held a second copy of a vocabulary the public page already owned

                    P3's console item was two promises in one sentence -- "no hardcoded copy, and the operator surfaces stay
                    `noindex`" -- and neither half had a reader. This unit adds one (`scripts/check_console_i18n.mjs`) and
                    reports what it found rather than what it expected.

                    WHAT IT READS. Every `page.tsx` under `apps/web/app`, in two passes. The noindex pass is console-only and
                    asks the question the root layout makes necessary: `apps/web/app/layout.tsx` sets
                    `robots: { index: true, follow: true }` site-wide, so a page under `app/admin/` or `app/merchant/` is
                    offered to search engines unless it overrides that in its own `generateMetadata`. The copy pass runs over
                    every page and reports a CJK ideograph that no comment covers. Measured: 31 `page.tsx` -- 20 console (9
                    under `app/admin`, 11 under `app/merchant`) and 11 public -- 20 of 20 console pages declaring the
                    override, and one offender.

                    THE OFFENDER, AND WHY IT WAS ONE. `apps/web/app/merchant/settings/page.tsx` carried a private
                    `WEEKDAY_LABELS` table holding two locales and a vocabulary of its own: it spelled the week 星期日 and
                    `Sunday`, while the public merchant page renders the same `business_hours` rows through `weekdayLabel` in
                    `apps/web/src/lib/format.ts`, which spells them 週日. So the same seven rows read one way on the
                    console and another way on the public page, and the console's table was a second copy that nothing
                    compared to the first. The page now calls the shared helper; the private table is gone.

                    THE VISIBLE COST, stated rather than buried: the console's hours list reads 週日 where it read
                    星期日. That is a copy change on an operator surface and it is deliberate -- it is the vocabulary the
                    public page already renders -- but it is a change a reviewer should be able to reverse, which is why it
                    is written down here rather than called a refactor.

                    WITNESS. `apps/web/src/lib/format.test.ts` is new and is that module's first test: it pins the three
                    locale tables, the wrap (7 -> the first day, -1 -> the last), the zh-HK default, the English fallback for
                    a locale the table does not hold, and the empty label for a day that is not a number. Measured: 8 passed
                    of 8 in 1.76 s. Without it the fix would be witnessed only by the absence of a character, which would not
                    notice a helper that returned nothing at all.

                    RE-MEASURED ON THESE BYTES. The census goes 1 offender -> 0 and exits 0; `npx tsc --noEmit` under
                    `apps/web` exits 0; step 7 exits 0 (174 source files, 26 read sites, 12 cited files); step 8 exits 0;
                    step 9 is unchanged at 80 tokens across 23 files, PASS -- the new files' docblocks contribute no
                    citation-shaped token, which was checked rather than assumed, because step 9 censuses comments in exactly
                    the extensions this unit added.

                    THE REFUSAL ARMS, because a reader that cannot refuse is not a check: `--plane` pointed at an empty
                    directory exits 2 with "no page.tsx was read ... nothing was censused, so nothing can be reported green";
                    an unknown option exits 2 naming the two flags this reader takes; a bare positional exits 2. No arm
                    prints a stack trace.

                    RESIDUES, named not fixed. (a) `apps/web/src/lib/format.ts`'s own header says it is "unit-tested in
                    ./facts.test.ts and ./format.test.ts". Only the second now exists; `facts.test.ts` is absent from the
                    working tree and from every commit, so that sentence is still half-false. `format.ts` was not edited for
                    it because the file carries another lane's uncommitted changes. (b) The accessibility half of the plan's
                    item -- contrast, labels, landmarks, focus order -- is not measured by this unit or by anything else in
                    the repository. (c) The copy rule is a CJK rule: hardcoded copy written in Latin script is invisible to
                    it, and so is a string that is never user-visible. (d) `docs/PLAN.md` P3 says "21 pages now exist" for the

## 191. D185: the §30 uniqueness guard is named by four documents and implemented by none — two doorway pages insert cleanly at a passing quality score

                    P3's second item asked for two things to be confirmed against reality: `seo_pages.quality_score`
                    and the `data` uniqueness guard, "the anti-spam promise". One holds, one does not, and the

                    flips each term, `below_quality_bar` among them at a score of 0.420. Measured on these bytes:
                    `mvn -o test -Dtest=SeoReadTest` → `Tests run: 10, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0` in 11.32 s.

                    The uniqueness guard does not exist. It is named by four documents — GROWTH.md:33 ("no 100k pages
                    differing only by city name"), DATABASE.md:171 ("`data` ... real listings backing the page"),
                    MERCHANT.md:56 ("each page must carry unique real value"), and `SeoRepository.java:19` ("`data
                    jsonb` ... the §30 anti-doorway guard") — and by no code. Measured: no migration V2-V7 mentions
                    `seo_pages`; `pg_constraint` on that table holds exactly four rows (`seo_pages_pkey`,
                    `seo_pages_tenant_id_path_lang_key`, and the two foreign keys) plus one trigger (`set_updated_at`);

```
insert into seo_pages (tenant_id, path, kind, status, quality_score, data)
values (..., '/probe/restaurants', 'category', 'published', 0.900, '{"listings":[{"merchant_id":"aaa"}]}'),
       (..., '/probe/cafes',       'category', 'published', 0.900, '{"listings":[{"merchant_id":"aaa"}]}');
        path        | quality_score |             data_md5
--------------------+---------------+----------------------------------
 /probe/cafes       |         0.900 | 1201fed4db4f2df819d27153f3f6484f
 /probe/restaurants |         0.900 | 1201fed4db4f2df819d27153f3f6484f
```

## 196. D190: step 13 stopped reporting one reader's pair and started reporting three, with the difference computed rather than remembered

What D188 established was a rule — a plane knob relocates the text it censuses and never the source index,
because every reader builds that index from the tree it was started in. What step 13 did with the rule was
asymmetric: 13b ran the ledger reader twice and printed both counts, while 13a and 13c ran theirs once and
printed one leg, so two of the three "committed plane" headings were a single measurement wearing a general
claim. And 13b's own line printed `77 / 0` and `65 / 41` and asked the reader to notice the difference by eye.

Now every leg runs its reader twice — this directory plus the step's own knob aimed at the worktree, and inside
the worktree with no knob — and one line per leg prints both counts and their subtraction. Measured at the same
commit: jsonb reads 12 files and 8 false sites against 10 and 11, so the index alone is worth 3 offenders there;
ledger citations 77 and 0 against 65 and 41, worth 41; comment citations 21 files with 0 offenders against 21
files with 10. Three readers, three pairs, one direction, and the direction is now a number the gate computes.

The extraction is where the honesty lives, and it is deliberately fussy. A count is pulled out of a run's own
census line, and when the line is absent the field prints `no-count` rather than 0 — 0 is a verdict about
citations, `no-count` is a verdict about the tool. Offender headers (`FALSE SITES (N)`, `FILE NOT FOUND (N)`)
are read when present; when they are absent the leg reports 0 only if the reader printed the sentence it prints
instead of a header, and `no-verdict` otherwise, so a reader that died mid-run cannot be transcribed as a clean
one. The subtraction refuses to operate on words and says so. A negative result would be printed as negative:
that would mean the knob leg is redder than a clean checkout, which is an anomaly to go looking for, not a
number to clamp.

Witnesses, both kinds, because a text predicate is satisfiable by a helper that never computed anything:

  · five arms in the harness that owns step 8's seam. The wiring arm asks for three knob captures, three bare
    captures, three `reconcile` calls and a helper body holding no digit — a number typed into the reporting
    line is a count the step remembers instead of one it measured. Four mutation arms run that identical
    predicate over copies: legs put back to the main tree, a count replaced by a literal, one leg's call
    deleted, a knob leg repointed inside the worktree. All four went red as predicted; the wiring arm holds.
  · two behavioural arms that cut the helper text out of the shipped gate, write it under the gate's own
    `set -euo pipefail`, and run it through bash over synthetic reader output. The header pair has to print
    12/8 against 10/11 with a gap of 3; the crashed leg has to print `no-verdict` and stop the subtraction.
    Both held. A separate probe of the helpers took every branch of the offender reader by hand: crash text,
    three different clean sentences, a header, words in the subtraction, and a negative gap.

Harness and step readings after the change, all on the working-copy plane: `falsify_ledger_text.mjs` 36 arms ·
35 held · 1 missed; step 8 `--worktree` 366 sections, 84 distinct files cited, 0 offenders; step 9 PASS with 88
comment-plane citations across 27 files and its own harness 13 of 13; step 7's seam harness 8 of 8; step 10
PASS, STATUS 151 headings at HEAD against 164 on disk and DECISIONS 165 against 177, nothing missing, nothing
duplicated; the blank-line census and step 8 agree on 14/14 at HEAD. Two reds are not this lane's and are
reported rather than edited: the missed arm is another lane's uncommitted section citing an empty line, and
`check_status_citations.mjs` names six spelled citations in the plan document that point at sections existing
only on disk. Step 13 remains a reporting step: the committed plane's redness is other lanes' uncommitted
sources, and only those lanes can move it. `bash -n` clean on the gate. Appends pure addition, zero lone LF.
Nothing pushed.

## 198. D192: step 9's offender belt read a count no plane it uses ever prints, so every green it gave was vacuous

D191's rule, one reader later: a rule that cannot fire on the plane the gate reads is not a
rule the gate has. Step 9 treats step 8's exit code as the verdict and claims a second reader as
a belt — it scrapes an offender count out of the child's report and requires zero. That wording
is produced by one line in step 8, guarded by "not the worktree mode", and every step 9 run goes
through the text mode, which sets worktree mode internally.

worktree mode the gate runs, one on the default plane — the only one step 9 never asks for. An
empty list passes every-style-true by construction, so the belt agreed with whatever step 8
printed, while the comment above it claimed a nonzero count would be caught there.

Fix in two halves: step 8 prints the strict plane's own count once in every mode, so the number
behind the exit code is in the report that produced it; step 9 reads exactly that number and
exits 2 — its code for "not a verdict" — unless it finds exactly one carrier. Zero means the
producer renamed the line or died early; two means the report mixes planes. Neither is
cleanliness now. The floor comes from the same scan it protects.

The seam and its witness: step 9 takes a checker path, and the harness forwards it to every arm
— D165's lesson that a mutant arm needs a real interface. Thirteen arms became seventeen, all
held. Renaming the carrier out of a copy of step 8 turns the control, the other flag spelling,
the past-EOF arm, the mixed plane and the carrier arm into the refusal they used to skip, while
the refusal arms stay green. That is the behavioral witness: the floor fires on a
runtime-equivalent mutation, not on a crash.

a nonexistent file — throw out of the grammar slice, exit 1, this directory's code for "a
citation is wrong", D159's class re-enacted minutes after the flag was added; it refuses with 2
and names the file now. Step 9's pass-through filter dropped the offender detail, so a red run
printed "see the report above" above a report whose only informative line had been filtered out;
the FAIL was true and unreadable. The filter keeps the empty-line sentence now.

blank lines — the gate script's note about where the reader's root comes from, and step 8's
header note about which flag spelling the comment census uses. Both were reported by shipped
readers, the second in the middle of the unit, and both repointed to derived numbers.

## 199. D193: step 7's census excused every miss with one bucket and answered its own parse failures in the verdict's exit code

D192's rule applied to the next reader: a rule that cannot fire on the plane the gate reads is not a

site cites no file, the file is outside the roots the scan walks, and the file is here and walked and
the key text is not in it — and printed nothing that told them apart. The roots themselves were
hard-coded, so a claim about what narrowing them would report could not be made false from outside
the shipped bytes.

(outside-the-census-roots, via `CENSUS COVERAGE — N answer(s)`, whose number joins the exit term);
one of them a report at exit 0 because only a human can say whether a read went through a helper.

census that opened no file is refused, and a census that opened files and found no read is refused,
because a scanner that finds nothing cannot contradict an answer list, it can only agree with it.

root adds no read today; apps/ai/nexus_ai alone opens 44 files and finds 0 reads, which the second

The belt and its honest limit. Three classes are plane facts and each promises in print that the site

absent-file rule silenced, run through the harness's `--reader` seam, while the shipped arms assert

The exit-code half of the unit. Five setup failures were `throw new Error`, which prints a stack and

Twenty-seven arms, all held on the final bytes. Control census on this tree: 22 answer rows, 31

ledger offenders in the uncommitted DECISIONS D188 and STATUS 191 sections, and 6 spelled STATUS

## 200. D194: step 7's census could print a reason and exit 0 over it, and its harness called a death a verdict by the header line

Three rules this unit moved from prose into the exit code, and one correction to this lane's own committed
record. The gate's reading steps certify a directory, not a commit, and the same distinction runs inside a single
run: a sentence that prints without changing the exit code certifies nothing.

**(a) `ANSWER KINDS UNUSED`.** The census expects four answer kinds and already noticed when a kind no row on the
plane carries was still expected — then exited 0 anyway. The branchless kinds now join the reason count
(`scripts/check_jsonb_reads.mjs:899-902`, block at `:819-827`), so a branch that classifies no row reddens the
gate instead of narrating itself. Its plant moves one row's kind word and nothing else; measured on it the census
counts are unchanged and exactly one reason appears.

**(b) A crash guard keyed on the last line instead of the first.** `scripts/falsify_quality_seam.mjs` decided
"the reader died" from the census's header — the first thing a reader prints — so a reader that died mid-report
was a finished run. The guard now reads a terminal sentinel that also declares the code the process intends
(`scripts/falsify_quality_seam.mjs:264`, reader `scripts/check_jsonb_reads.mjs:902`), and a run whose declared
code the process does not take is a crash, not a verdict. The `expectCrash` flag is policed both ways: an arm that
declares a death over a run that finished reddens through the same predicate the loop uses
(`scripts/falsify_quality_seam.mjs:584-586`).

**(c) The `--quality` seam refuses instead of dying.** After D159 made a mistyped flag value a legal request, a
path with no file behind it and a path that is a directory both reached `readFileSync` and ended in `node:fs`
frames at exit 1 — the code for "a read or a site is wrong". Both are exit-2 refusals naming the thing handed to
it (`scripts/check_jsonb_reads.mjs:99-107`), and their arms assert the sentence, not only the code.

**(d) The correction: my own D193 citations were mis-aimed, and step 8 cannot see it.** D193's edits were
line insertions, so all eight line numbers its entry cites in these two files moved. Step 8 checks that a cited
file has the cited line — its printed LIMITS say it cannot check that the line says what the sentence claims — so
the drift was invisible to the gate that certified the append. The re-aimed numbers were derived by reading
HEAD's text at each cited line and matching it against the final bytes where the match is unique; one of them was
a bare continuation (`(:557)`) inheriting its filename across a line wrap, and at HEAD it pointed at an empty
line. The audit that found it carries filename state across lines, because a hard-wrapped ledger cannot otherwise
be audited honestly. Nine further citations into these two files live in other lanes' sections and were already
false at HEAD; they are named, not rewritten — the fix belongs to whoever owns the claim.

Witnesses, all against the shipped bytes, one rule removed at a time (`.scratch/d194_meta.mjs`, run on the final

Plane for these bytes: the two scripts this unit edits, and the two ledger sections it lands. Step 7 and its
harness were measured on the final code bytes before the ledger went in; steps 8, 9, 10 and 12 and the committed

by hand between reader and harness, so a one-sided rename is a loud crash rather than a derived check; and a run

## 201. D195: two readers nothing ran, three CI steps that could not fail, and two counts in this unit’s own
prose that only a run could correct
The rule this lane has now earned five times (D98, D150-D152, D191, D192) is that a rule which cannot fire on
the plane it is read on is not a rule the gate has. This unit reads that rule back at the readers themselves, and
at the two kinds of place that run them. Both classes were FALSE on the bytes this pass started from, and every
number below is quoted out of the census’s own output rather than out of a plan.
(A) REACHABILITY. `scripts/` holds ten first-party `check_*.mjs`; two were invoked by no surface at all — not
`scripts/db_gate_fresh.sh`, not `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, not the `Makefile`. They were
`scripts/check_console_i18n.mjs` (the copy and noindex promises: 31 `page.tsx` censused, 20 console, 20 declaring
`index: false`, 0 inline-copy offenders) and `scripts/check_console_a11y.mjs` (landmarks, accessible names, focus
order, printed contrast: 20 console pages, 1 `<main>` carrying `id="nexus-main"`, 2/2 named `<nav>`, 24 controls
with a name, 0 positive `tabindex`, 10 ratios recomputed, tightest 4.80:1). Both PASSED and nothing ran either;
`docs/PLAN.md` recorded the accessibility half of P3 as "unmeasured" while the census that measures it sat in the
tree. Both run in gate step 14 and in the workflow now, and so does `scripts/falsify_console_a11y.mjs` (13 of 13
arms). The census prints `invoked by 10 of 10 (unreached: 0)`.
(B) PIPES. A reader whose exit code travels through a pipe is read through the pipe’s exit code, and a pipeline
reports its LAST command unless the shell holds it. `scripts/db_gate_fresh.sh:51` is what holds this repository’s
own pipes together, and D150/D151’s proof that step 11 can stop the run is a proof about that one line; GitHub
Actions does not hold them, and its documented default for a `run:` step on Linux is `bash -e {0}`
(workflow-syntax reference, the shell table: unspecified -> `bash -e {0}`; `shell: bash` -> `bash --noprofile
--norc -eo pipefail {0}`). Three steps in this workflow pipe a checker into `tee` (.github/workflows/ci.yml:215-236)
so that the report is an artifact, and none of them declared a shell, so none of them could fail. Measured in a
shell rather than argued: `false | tee /dev/null` exits 0 under `bash -e` and 1 under `bash -eo pipefail`. All three
declare `shell: bash` now, under a note that says why (.github/workflows/ci.yml:200), and the census prints
`7 step(s) pipe a checker into tee` with 0 UNPROTECTED.
(C) TWO COUNTS IN THIS UNIT’S OWN PROSE WERE WRONG, AND RUNNING A FILE CORRECTED BOTH. The note written above the
piped steps said three steps "carried Hard-fail in their own comments". One of the three does; one of the other two
annotates itself "Report mode for now", which is the opposite claim; the third describes a verdict without that
word. Rather than re-type the number it is DERIVED now: the census reads each step’s own comment and prints
`hard-fail claims 1 of 7 piped step(s) say "hard fail" in their own comment: jsonb keys read by the build, against
the declared list` (scripts/check_reader_reachability.mjs:155,:189-190). Writing that field exposed a second defect
that reading the file had not: the step splitter put each step’s comment block at the TAIL of the PREVIOUS block,
so the one step whose comment says "Hard-fail" was reported under the NAME of the step before it — an offender a
person would go and fix, naming a different step. Each block’s trailing comment run is carried forward to the step
it describes now (scripts/check_reader_reachability.mjs:121-137), and a blank line ends the run, which is how the
job-level note stays a note about the job rather than about the next step.
(D) THE OWED HALF OF D193. Step 13’s 13a and 13c legs carried plane-shaped environment prefixes
(`GATE_QUALITY_SQL="$WT/data/seed/quality.sql"`, `GATE_COMMENT_PLANE="$WT"`) in front of harnesses that read no
environment variable at all — verified by grepping all seven `scripts/falsify_*.mjs` for `process.env`: none of

(E) THE NEW READER’S OWN ARGUMENTS. `scripts/check_reader_reachability.mjs` parses its flags with
`scripts/cli_args.mjs` rather than with a private loop; its first version was a second copy of the one thing that

`scripts/falsify_flag_dialect.mjs` names this reader among the ones on the shared parser
(scripts/falsify_flag_dialect.mjs:303), so a silent revert to a private loop is a red in that census.
WITNESSES, all against the shipped bytes. `node scripts/check_reader_reachability.mjs` exits 0.

STATED LIMITS, because a census that hides its blind spots is what this project keeps catching. The three surfaces

## 202. D196: the harness scored the checker's vocabulary from three lists typed by hand, and the checker could file a miss under a class it had no sentence for and exit 0 over it

The rule chain this unit extends: D193 — a rule that cannot fire on the plane the gate reads is not a rule the
gate has; D194 — a rule that fires, prints, and reaches no exit code is not a rule the gate has either; D196 —
**a copy of another file's vocabulary is not that file's vocabulary**, and it goes stale in silence, because the
stale copy still prints green.

Closed in the checker. Its classifier could file a row under a class `MISS_WHY` has no entry for, print
`<class> (N): no stated reason`, and join nothing — the mirror of the defect D194 fixed one block further down,
named by D194's own comment ("the second direction of vocabulary drift"), which is how it was found: reading the
sentence the last unit wrote. It is now `NO STATED REASON (N row(s) across M class(es))` and its rows join the exit
term beside the other six (scripts/check_jsonb_reads.mjs:801-812, scripts/check_jsonb_reads.mjs:899-900).

Closed in the harness. `MISS_CLASSES` (5 typed names), `VERDICT_MARKS` (6 typed strings) and `TERMINAL` (a regex
retyped from the checker's sentinel sentence) are now read out of the reader this harness instance points at: the
class names come from its `MISS_WHY` block and are cross-checked against the reasons its classifier pushes, the two
populations the checker itself compares at run time; the verdict heads are its `console.log` literal prefixes, with
the refusal's own print excluded by the property of the source line that makes it a refusal (`process.exit(2)` on
it) rather than by a name typed here; the terminal pattern is the reader's last template line with each
interpolation turned into a capture group, floored at three groups. `onlyClass()` refuses to build an arm aimed at
a class the reader never files, and the report prints the vocabulary it scored (`DERIVED VOCABULARY`), because a
count over a set nobody can see is a number and not a measurement.

Why each mattered, in one line each. A typed class list goes blind on a rename: the planted row counts as nothing,
and the arm reports the miss it was written to catch as though it had caught it. A six-string marks list goes blind
in the direction with teeth: the checker prints more verdict lines than six, so a refusal that also answered —
through `UNDECLARED`, `WRONG TABLE`, `NO KIND`, `CALLED NEVER-READ`, `EVERY READ THE SCAN FOUND`,
`ANSWERS THE READ CENSUS DID NOT FIND` — read as total. A retyped sentinel regex fails loudly but expensively: a
reword stops the match, `crashed` becomes true for every run, and the arms report deaths that never happened.

Reachability. No answer plant can unnamed a class, so the witness is a mutant reader with one `MISS_WHY` key
renamed: the same fixture is rc 0 over the shipped reader and must not print the block; over the renamed reader it
is rc 1 and must, with the sentinel declaring exactly one reason. The pre-existing hand-judged-class arm carries
the absence half, so the charge cannot leak onto a described class: policed both ways, reachable in one.

The derivation's first run printed one head too many — a prose footer (`LIMITS, stated rather than implied:`)
shared the shape of a verdict — and the printed population is what made it visible. A hand list cannot be wrong in
a way anyone can see; a derived list is wrong in public and gets fixed the same day, which is what happened here.
A head is now the capitals run only: it ends at the first lower-case letter, and what is left must not end on
sentence punctuation. The footer that broke the first version is kept as the arm's plant, found by a property of
the print that *follows* it — a quoted `console.log` opening in a lower-case letter can only be the second half of
a sentence — so the plant moves with the reader's prose instead of being a copy of it. Two arms run the pair: a
refusal that answers through a head the six strings never carried must be seen (the hand-typed copy reddens here),
and a refusal that prints only its disclaimer must not be (an over-wide derivation reddens here). The test lives
in an arm and not in an import-time refusal because a `die` would preempt the arm that names the case, and an arm
no run can redden is a caption.

Witnesses, seven legs, each removing exactly one rule this unit added, run over the final bytes in
`.scratch/d196_meta.mjs`, and every leg's prediction was written before it ran. Take the unnamed rows back out of
the exit term and exactly the unnamed-class arm reddens (rc 1, 1 arm). Put the six hand-typed marks back and run
over the shipped reader and exactly the answer-arm reddens (1 arm) — the short list is blind, not over-wide. Run
the derived marks against a reader whose refusal also answers and all seven totality arms redden (7 arms), which
is the measured size of the hole the six strings left. Re-type the terminal regex while rewording the reader's
sentinel and 16 arms report deaths that never happened: the pre-D196 count exactly, because the two arms added
here score rc-2 refusals, which a broken terminal cannot turn into a crash. Hand-type a class the reader never
files and the harness refuses at import rather than run an unfalsifiable arm. Remove the capitals-run cut and
exactly the prose arm reddens (1 arm). Aim the prose-footer finder away from the footer and it refuses at import,
because a plant that cannot be built is not a witness. Seven of seven matched.

The unit's own blast radius, because a rule that moves the ground under its own record is still a rule. This unit
inserted 12 lines in the checker and 170 in its harness and deleted two named constants; of the 25 live citation
numbers in D193, D194 and STATUS §200, 16 had slid off the sentence they belong to, 4 named a thing this unit
deleted, and 5 were already right — 16 ledger lines rewritten to correct them. Step 8 only asks that a cited line
exists, so the gate was green over every one of the 16. The corrections are derived at landing, not copied from a
previous run: a number must match one line's content in the working copy, a range must match its whole block
contiguously, and the one block that no longer sits contiguously is the exit term this unit edited from the inside,

Caught during this landing, by a guard that worked. The step 9 falsifier refused this run with exit 2: a comment in

## 203. D197: the directory exclusion had no name for the lane's own scratch, and the classifier dropped every path cite that began with a dot

Two hiding places, one clause apart, both found while arming the first. `VENDOR_DIRS` never named `.scratch`,
so the three readers walked a lane's working directory as part of the repository: D196 had left a stale copy of
`cli_args.mjs` under `.scratch/d194_meta/`, the shared walker returned that basename twice, a citation naming
exactly one shipped file read AMBIGUOUS, gate step 9's falsifier refused with exit 2, and because
`db_gate_fresh.sh` runs under `set -euo pipefail` that refusal stops whichever session runs the gate next.
The list is now the union of the two drifted lists (22 names, `VENDOR_DIRS` in `scripts/source_index.mjs`), `.scratch` among
them. D196's residue — "nothing charges the write" — is answered by `scripts/falsify_ledger_text.mjs:701`,
which keeps out of the exclusion any file that turns out to be tracked, so the name cannot become a hiding
place for a first-party claim.

The bigger one was found by arming the smaller. `isCitation` (`scripts/check_ledger_citations.mjs:404`) asked
its bare-dotfile rule about names that also carry a slash, and that rule consults `BY_BASENAME`, which is
keyed on basenames and never on paths. It cannot hold one, so every citation whose path begins with a dot
directory was dropped before reaching `resolve()` — not judged, not reported, invisible in the counts because
a dropped token is still a token. Ten such tokens sit in the two ledgers at this commit: four to
`.github/workflows/ci.yml` and six to `./.gitignore`, the root-relative form the resolver has a branch for and
the CI form the arms cite. None had been judged by any run since D88 wrote the classifier. The path clause is
now asked first and judged on its last segment (`scripts/check_ledger_citations.mjs:409`), so `./.gitignore:21`
is a citation and `some/dir/notes` stays prose.

Both halves were measured rather than argued. The ten-token count came out of this file's own tokenizer and
its own `isCitation` read back off its bytes; a hand-written regex over the same two documents printed 4, which
is the reason the number in the checker's comment says where it came from. Three checks had to pass before the
name went into the list: `git grep -F '.scratch'` over tracked code returns nothing (the ten hits a first pass
printed were the English phrase "from scratch", produced by an unescaped dot in a regex, not a path); the
comment reader aimed at that directory prints `COMMENT CITATIONS: 0 tokens found`, which is this project's
refusal for an empty plane and not a green; and excluding the directory costs 73 indexable files, all of them
under a directory literally named `.scratch`, none tracked.

Eight arms went into the harness (50 total, 50 held, exit 0): a cite into an excluded directory is charged even
though the harness proves the file is on disk; the same plant text over two index roots that differ only in
which directory the twin sits in comes out resolved on one and AMBIGUOUS on the other, which is D196's failure
written as a prediction instead of a story; a basename whose twin is excluded resolves to the shipped file; a
dot-directory path cite is counted and judged; the census prints the shared set's own size rather than a copy
of it; the membership predicate reddens on the same list with D197's name lifted; and a mirror walk that must
first reproduce the shipped index file for file (592 entries) before its radius claim is believed.

Residue, stated because the arms do not close it. First, the harness is not stable under load: six runs of the
50 arms, four green, two red on different arms, and in both reds the child process printed nothing at all —
one exit 134, one empty — while the identical invocation standalone returns the expected verdict. `run()`
reports an unread child as an arm result instead of refusing, so a loaded host can turn a green reader into a
false statement about it; that is the same class as D194's "a death called a verdict", one level up, and it is
the next unit here. Second, the write-time charge is partial: the index holds 592 files under 513 basenames,
and 27 basenames are held by more than one file (31 of them `page.tsx`), so charging duplicates at write time
means distinguishing a name a citation can actually land on from a name the tree structure repeats.

## 204. D198: a dead child was filed as a verdict about the reader, and the first guard written against it could not be falsified five ways

D197 closed with this unit named: `run()` returned `{code, out}` and the reporting loop scored every arm from
those two fields, so a child that died before printing anything — exit 134 from an abort, or an empty stdout —
arrived as `MISSED exit 2 expected, 134 printed` with an empty verdict line, and again as `exit 0 expected, 0
printed`: both of them findings about a reader no arm had reached. Six runs of the 50 arms on a loaded host had
gone four green and two red, each red a different arm, while the same invocation standalone returned its expected
verdict. Both halves of that sentence are armed now. A child gets three attempts (scripts/falsify_ledger_text.mjs:217), an exit code
is believed only when stdout carried something, and the reporting loop refuses the whole run with exit 2 and
`unread N of M arms` (scripts/falsify_ledger_text.mjs:879) rather than scoring an observation nobody made. The refusal is scoped by a
`reading` tag (scripts/falsify_ledger_text.mjs:473) so the three stub arms that are deliberately aimed at silent children cannot trip it.
The contract in the header says all three exit-2 causes out loud, because a harness whose exit codes are not in
its own documentation is one more thing to rediscover (scripts/falsify_ledger_text.mjs:87).

The structural half is what keeps "stdout is empty" from being a guess. An empty stdout is a death rather than a
verdict only if the reader prints before it can exit, so that is read out of the reader's own bytes — every
`process.exit(` in `scripts/check_ledger_citations.mjs` has a `console.log(` before it — and armed against a copy
of the reader with an exit hoisted above its first print. Measured by hand against a silent stub, the refusal
prints `unread 32 of 49 arms` and exits 2; the 49 is every arm in a non-mutant run, and the 32 is every arm that
had a reader to hear from.

Most of the work was that the guard arrived half-written in the working copy. Measured as it stood: 56 arms · 48
held · 8 missed. Five of the eight were defects in that half-finished guard, and each is a shape this file exists
to catch in other people's readers. (a) The attempt counter reported four attempts for three — the loop index was
incremented by the loop and then incremented again on the way out — and the arm that names `attempts 3`, the only
arm that could see it, was red. (b) The arm pinning that stderr is not the verdict channel demanded
`a death rattle on stderr` in its must-list while printing a summary string that could not contain it, so it
reddened on its own wording; the child's own text is carried in the arm's evidence now. (c) The "prints before it
exits" arm compared the byte offsets of the first print and the first exit and printed a line its own regex could
not match, so its evidence and its prediction were two different claims; it asks what the claim means now, with
the number of exits that have no print before them as the measurement. (d) The copy that is supposed to witness
that predicate had its ternary inverted, so it could only be red when the predicate was TRUE — a mutation witness
that cannot redden on the mutation it plants. (e) The refusal those six arms predict did not exist, which is the
one arm that was red for the right reason.

Finished and re-measured: 56 arms · 56 held · 0 missed, exit 0, three consecutive runs over the same bytes with
Git's bash first on `PATH`. The three remaining misses in the as-found run were not defects in this file and are
not fixed here: `bash` on this host resolves to `C:\WINDOWS\system32\bash.exe`, the WSL launcher, which cannot

One blast radius, measured rather than assumed. This unit inserts 160 lines and deletes 9 in

## 206. D201: the reader that asks whether a cited line still holds the text it was chosen for

Gate step 8 has four classes for a line-number citation and every one of them is about presence — the file is
missing, the basename is ambiguous, the number is past EOF, the line is blank. STATUS §203 recorded this lane
naming the `VENDOR_DIRS` declaration by a line number that stood two lines high on the day the sentence was
written and nineteen lines high after 0418b22, and no class of step 8 can see that: the pointed-at line exists and
still holds text. `scripts/check_line_cite_drift.mjs` is the reader for the class. It takes each citation in the
committed ledgers, blames the ledger line that holds it to the commit which wrote it, reads the cited file at that
commit and at HEAD, and compares the text of the cited line. Content equality between two refs is derivable;
"does this sentence still describe that line" is not, and the reader never asks it.

Measured on this lane's plane, before this section existed: 416 citation-shaped tokens in 22,088 ledger lines, all
416 blamed to an author. 262 of them name a bare basename, which this reader counts as UNPATHED and refuses to
resolve, and 12 name no file at HEAD — step 8's FILE NOT FOUND, reported as NOT-AT-HEAD and not judged twice. That
leaves 142 judged by content: 100 EXACT, 24 MOVED, 17 GONE, 1 NO-BASE. MOVED is the unambiguous one — the text the
citation named is still in the file, only at a different line, so the ledger's number is stale — and the reader's
strict mode exits 1 on it, which is why the CI step runs in report mode: 24 stale numbers are a cleanup this lane
did not make. GONE is where a reworded comment lands beside a deleted target, indistinguishable without reading
meaning, so it is a queue. The single NO-BASE row cites a line of `scripts/falsify_ledger_text.mjs` that the
committed file does not have, which is a citation committed against bytes that were still uncommitted — another
lane's text, reported and not edited.

`scripts/falsify_line_cite_drift.mjs` arms it in 8 cases, each a throwaway repository rather than a mutation of
this tree, because `scripts/` belongs to two lanes at once: the control plane, MOVED by an insertion above the
target, GONE by a reworded target, NO-BASE by a citation that predates its own code, the two counted-not-judged
classes meeting the read-nothing floor, the flag refusals, and the plane guard. 8/8 MATCHED. Two of them were not
free. The harness derives its verdict vocabulary from the reader's own counts declaration, and its first run read
eight sites in a class that had none, because the summary sentence said "step 8 of the gate" and a per-class scan
takes the first digit it finds — the printout is now one verdict line per class and a missing line stops the run.
The shallow-plane arm passed at first for the wrong reason: a local `git clone --depth 1` silently ignores
`--depth`, so the plane the arm believed was shallow was a full clone and the guard was never struck; with the
transport forced, the reader computes a confident EXACT on a history it cannot date and exit 2 refuses it.
`actions/checkout@v4` defaults to depth 1, so the drift step's job now fetches the whole history, and the guard is
what would make that knob's absence visible instead of quiet.

Not decided here: the 24 MOVED and 17 GONE citations stay as they are, and a ratchet that forbids new drift needs a
baseline the scan itself produces rather than a number typed into a flag. Task #126 — reconciling a ledger's
numeric claim about the code with the code — is this same missing reader aimed at figures instead of positions.
One more, self-inflicted and caught by the reader on the commit that landed it. The 24 MOVED above was
measured before the drift step's own job landed, and the four lines that job's fetch-depth note occupies in
`.github/workflows/ci.yml` moved two citations in this ledger that name lines of that file — so the same command,
re-run on the landing, prints 26 MOVED and 98 EXACT. Both were re-aimed in the same breath, which is the first time
this lane has used the reader on its own commit, and it is the census counting its own counter one file further
along: a drift census is not exempt from the drift it reports.


`check_line_cite_drift.mjs` judges a `file:line` by asking whether the text it was written against is still
at that line. Task #126 asked for the same reader aimed at **figures instead of positions**, and the size of
the problem came from a census before any code was written:

```
     63 216 assertions
     34 216 quality checks
     23 216 checks
```

**`216` is written 120 times in these two ledgers and linked to nothing.** Add one check to the gate and 120
sentences go stale with nothing reddening — the same failure this repository has met in three other shapes
(a declared jsonb read whose key stopped shipping, a route no service serves, a citation aimed at a line that
no longer holds its text).

`scripts/check_ledger_numbers.mjs` is the census half, and it is deliberately two-sided:

```
node scripts/check_ledger_numbers.mjs --top 5
  claims read              967 over docs/DECISIONS.md, docs/STATUS.md
  nouns known              11
  assertions       newest    216  docs/STATUS.md:8434
                   values 216×63 · 214×18 · 213×1 · 22×1 · 20×1 · 12×1 · … 3 more
                   answered by the gate’s own printout
RESULT: UNCHECKED — no expectation given, so no claim was judged.   exit 2
```

**It refuses to judge without a source for the number.** "I have no idea what the right number is" and "the
number is right" must not print the same way, so `--expect "assertions=216"` is the only thing that produces
a verdict, and it judges exactly one claim: the newest section's.

**The first verdict, from a real gate run** (`TMPDIR=/tmp` exported, 15m39s):

```
5/12  data/seed/quality.sql   -> 217 quality checks passed (tables=58, migrations=8)
6/12  seed_truncate_probe.sh     RESULT: PASS
7/12  check_jsonb_reads.mjs      RESULT: NOT CHECKED   EXIT=2

node scripts/check_ledger_numbers.mjs --expect "assertions=216"  → MATCHED     exit 0
node scripts/check_ledger_numbers.mjs --expect "assertions=217"  → MISMATCHED  exit 1
```

**The gate now files 217 assertions**, measured 2026-09-30 on a from-scratch schema of 58 tables and eight
migrations — stated here as a claim rather than only quoted in the evidence block below, because a number
inside a fence is a record of what a tool printed and not a sentence this ledger is asserting. The claim at
`docs/STATUS.md:8434` sits in §154, which is a dated record of a run made when 216 was true — so it stays as
written, and the current number is stated here instead. That is the append-only rule applied to a figure:
a number written when it was right is not a lie, and rewriting it would destroy the only evidence of when it
changed. The residue is a claim, not a correction: **217, measured 2026-09-30 on a from-scratch schema of 58
tables and 8 migrations.**

**Its first bug was its own, and the first run found it.** `newest` was "the last occurrence in reading
order", and because `DECISIONS.md` was read second, the newest claim about `checks` came back as **8**
(`docs/DECISIONS.md:9730`) — a number in a sentence about something else. Newest now means the latest
**section**, with `STATUS.md` read last because it is the ledger of record for where the build stands. The
same run also cost a rewrite of the flag handling: `cli_args.mjs` returns `{ok, value, flag}` and refuses a
value flag given twice, so `--expect` is comma-separated rather than repeatable — one dialect, as D158
intends.

**And step 7's red in that run is this sandbox, now said in the right words.** `falsify_quality_seam.mjs`
spawns a child node process for both planes; `spawnSync` returned `status: null` with `error.code` set, and
the verdict read only `the shipped plane is not green (rc null, control rc null)` — a sentence about the
plane, when the fact was about the environment. It now carries the reason:

```
before:  (rc null, control rc null)
after:   (rc null — the child could not be started: EBUSY, control rc null — the child could not be
          started: EBUSY)
```

`EBUSY`: the same restriction that makes `spawnSync git` fail on this machine (STATUS §86). So **gate steps
7-12 cannot run here at all**, and D198's guard — an exit code is believed only when stdout carried
something — is about a child that ran and died, which is a different event from a child that never started.
Both now have a sentence; neither is filed as a verdict about the reader.

Limits, stated rather than implied: the reader counts numbers, not meanings. `checks` still catches an
incidental "8 checks" in a sentence about arms, and `rows` mixes "4 rows" (a probe result) with "22,592
rows" (a corpus size). Only `assertions` is unambiguous today, and that is the noun to wire to a gate run
first.

## 207. D202: step 15 — the ledger's line-number drift reader runs in the gate, reporting whether citations still name the line they were written against

                    citation in the ledgers, blames the citing line to the commit that wrote it, reads the
                    cited file at THAT commit and at HEAD, and compares the text of line NN. It reports
                    seven classes: EXACT (text identical), MOVED (text survives at one new line), NOT-UNIQUE
                    (blank when written or multiple occurrences at HEAD), GONE (text nowhere at HEAD),
                    NO-BASE (line didn't exist at the commit), UNPATHED (basename-only cite), NOT-AT-HEAD
                    (rooted path absent at HEAD). The `--reaim` mode prints a derived re-aim list so a

                    NOT-AT-HEAD, NOT-UNIQUE blank, NOT-UNIQUE duplicate, --reaim, refusals, shallow-plane
                    refusal, NOT-UNIQUE reasons, --reaim rows) — 12/12 MATCHED.

## 210. D206: step 9's two exit-2 guards got arms by copying the reader into a temp scripts/ instead of mutating a shipped byte

                    D205 shipped two `RESULT: NOT RUN` guards and recorded in its own message that
                    neither had ever fired, because the harness could mutate step 8 but not step 9.
                    A guard nobody has seen red is a sentence about a floor. Step 9 turns out to be
                    mutatable without touching a shipped byte: it imports only two files from the
                    directory beside itself and takes its resolver as a flag, so a copy written into
                    a temp `scripts/`, aimed at the SHIPPED step 8 with `--checker` and at a fixture
                    plane with `--plane`, is a complete reader.

                    Four arms, predictions written before any mutant ran. C0 is the verbatim control
                    — the copy reads the plane the shipped reader reads, same exit, same named
                    offender — because without it an M-arm's red could belong to the relocation
                    rather than to the mutation. M1 deletes the bullet map so nothing places, which
                    makes the refusal the FIRST one, and the refusal has to count the bullets it
                    had. M2 keys the same map one line off: exit 1 and an author block naming the
                    good cite's line while the required line is absent. The line arithmetic is
                    load-bearing: a map off by one does not go quiet, it names the wrong comment
                    with full confidence, and that is the failure mode this unit exists to be able
                    to see. M3 needs a two-offender plane — one bullet placed, one outside — because
                    a lone offender that misses is the first guard's red, which is why the second
                    guard needed a plane the previous batch did not have.

                    M3 missed on its first run, and the miss was in the fixture rather than in the
                    guard: a plane whose every citation is a phantom never reaches an offender
                    verdict at all. Step 8 refuses with its own non-vacuity guard ("citation(s)
                    found and 0 file(s) resolved"), step 9 reports that the child produced no
                    report, and the run exits 2 — for the reason of the OTHER guard. An arm scored
                    on its exit code alone would have called that a hold. The fixture now carries
                    one resolvable citation beside the two phantoms, and the arm requires guard 2's
                    exact sentence.

                    Measured: 22 arms · 22 held · 0 missed, exit 0, harness +88/-0 over 268 -> 356

## 219. D217: the gate prints its own step total, and nothing judges it — measured three ways, three answers

                    Step 17 was filed to catch exactly one class: a number the ledger states that the
                    artefact it describes no longer states. It judges three nouns, and the nouns it does
                    not judge keep drifting in the open. One of them is the gate total, and this batch
                    measured it before asking anyone to agree.

                    What the working copy files: 21 step invocations, 17 distinct step numbers, and six
                    denominators in the labels themselves (12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17). The three are all
                    true of the same file, and none of them is what a reader would call its step count.
                    The invocation total is larger than the number total because a branch files both of
                    its legs as the same step number, and because three sub-labels share one number. The
                    denominators disagree with each other because a label is written once, when its own
                    step is the newest thing in the script, and is never revisited: the first twelve
                    still say they are one of twelve, while the last one says it is one of seventeen. So
                    the sentence in the header of a step is a numeric claim with no reader behind it, and
                    it has quietly gone stale five times in this file.

                    The ledger half of the same finding: the numbers census knows the noun steps, names
                    its carrier as the steps of the fresh-database gate, and has no expectation aimed at
                    it, so the newest claim it holds matches none of the three measured spellings.

                    What this batch deliberately does not do: it does not add a fourth expectation to
                    step 17. The numbers checker is a file no commit holds on this plane — another lane
                    is writing it live — so a derived value aimed at it would be a gate whose red can
                    only be reproduced against a draft no commit holds. The spelling decision
                    also has to be made by somebody: a numbered step, an invocation, or a label
                    denominator is three different nouns, and picking one in a commit message is how a
                    convention gets invented without a reader to enforce it. Both are owed work, and the
                    residue is recorded rather than guessed at here.

                    Recorded as the standing question for the next unit in this lane: the gate should
                    carry the total its own labels claim, derived from the file rather than typed into
                    it, and a step whose header says a different total than the script files should be
                    the arm that proves it. Appends pure addition, zero lone LF. Nothing pushed.

## 220. D218: a NOT-UNIQUE row is not always a stale number — one of ours names text the file legitimately holds twice

                    Step 16 has two remaining rows and the batch that cleared the ten MOVED cites left
                    these on purpose. Reading both sentences and the file they point into shows they are
                    not the same case, and that the remedy the step promises — re-aim by reading the
                    sentence — cannot work for one of them.

                    The cited expression in the STATUS row is the collateral computation. In the shipped
                    harness that line exists twice, at two different places that both need it: the per-arm
                    loop and the control-leg block. Neither is a copy-paste mistake and neither is stale,
                    so whichever number the ledger writes, the reader finds the same text on two lines and
                    calls it NOT-UNIQUE. The DECISIONS row is a range whose start line lands in the same
                    pair. That is why these two survived the re-aim batch rather than being part of it:
                    the drift reader derives a new number for a MOVED cite, and there is no number here
                    that would satisfy it.

                    So the class has a second, unrecorded member: a citation whose target text is
                    legitimately duplicated in the file. Three fates are possible and this unit declines
                    to choose one in prose — widen the citation to a span no other site shares, which the
                    reader would have to learn to compare as a span; make the ledger quote a fragment
                    unique to the intended occurrence, which loses the expression the sentence was about;
                    or have the reader accept a duplicated target when the sentence itself names which
                    block it means, which needs a spelling for block identity that no reader has yet.
                    Each of those is a change to a checker, and the checkers in this area are another
                    lane s live drafts, so the question is filed rather than implemented.

                    Measured on this plane after the re-aim batch and before this append: step 15 EXACT
                    127 with MOVED 0, step 16 RESULT FAIL on 2 NOT-UNIQUE of 147 judged, step 8 censises
                    HEAD strictly and counts the working copy, over 525 citations; step 10 PASS, step 12
                    PASS. Two of the ten re-aimed rows turned out to be ranges, and moving only the first
                    endpoint left a backwards span the working copy reports as its own two offenders —

                    Until that correction is committed, step 8 exits 1 on purpose: the two broken spans are

values; a future unit may wire the gate's own output directly". Step 5, by contrast, already passed the
count it had just measured. So the same quantity entered the gate twice — once derived, once typed — and
only the derived half could notice a change.

Now all three read the count step 5 filed, and the step refuses before judging when that count is not a
positive integer. The refusal matters: the error path prints the count as a question mark, and a
derivation reading a question mark would have produced an expectations string that quietly disagreed with
every ledger sentence while still being called a measurement.

Five arms, predictions written first, all matched:

- count 217 -> exit 0, RESULT: MATCHED, expectations line printed as the three derived nouns;
- count 216 -> exit 1, RESULT: MISMATCH on all three nouns. This is the arm that proves the derivation
  governs: the verdict moved because the measurement moved, not because an operator retyped a figure;
- count empty, count 0, count "?" -> exit 2 each, naming step 17 in the refusal.

One prediction was wrong and the error was mine, not the gate's: the first green arm returned exit 1 with
RESULT: MATCHED already printed. The slice I sourced into the harness ran past step 17 into step 18 and the
final summary, where an unbound variable stopped my scratch harness. Tightening the slice to end at the

## 224. the spawn-failure class, censused: six tools die without a verdict, and the pattern is one try/catch

`execFileSync` and `spawnSync` kept producing the same failure in three different costumes, and each costume
was diagnosed separately: `rc null` for both planes of `scripts/falsify_quality_seam.mjs`, a misleading
`exit 1` from `scripts/check_comment_citations.mjs` (because `err.status ?? 1` turns a `null` into a
plausible number), and an uncaught `spawnSync git EBUSY` that stopped `scripts/falsify_line_cite_drift.mjs`
with no RESULT line at all. So the class was censused rather than met a fourth time.

Every tool in `scripts/` that spawns a child, run on this machine and classified by whether it printed a
`RESULT:` line:

```
rc 0, verdict printed   check_citation_supports_sentence (CENSUS) · falsify_flag_dialect (PASS)
                        check_line_cite_drift (REPORT 127/147)
rc 2, refusal stated    check_ledger_sections · check_status_citations · falsify_reader_reachability
                        check_falsifier_registry (no --db) · falsify_quality_seam (EBUSY)
                        check_comment_citations (EBUSY) · check_ledger_citations
rc 1, FAIL stated       falsify_comment_plane (57 arms, 0 held) · falsify_untracked_cites
                        falsify_status_citations
rc 1, NO verdict line   citation_blank_census · citation_blank_sites · falsify_ledger_sections
                        falsify_ledger_text · falsify_line_cite_drift · falsify_plane_reads
rc 127, no verdict      falsify_console_a11y
```

**Six tools die without saying anything**, and every one does it the same way: a bare
`execFileSync('git'|'node'|'bash', ...)` with no guard at the call site. They are named rather than fixed
here, because each belongs to a lane still writing it, and a census that lists them is the queue.

**One is fixed, as the shape to copy.** `falsify_line_cite_drift.mjs` builds a real throwaway repository per
arm, so a machine that cannot start git cannot run any of them; its `g()` now catches the spawn and says so
instead of throwing past a top-level block that cannot catch it:

```
before:  an uncaught `spawnSync git EBUSY`, exit 1, no RESULT line
after:   RESULT: NOT CHECKED — this harness drives real throwaway repositories, and git could not be
         started: EBUSY.
           No arm below was run. A refusal is not a failure, and the two must not share a verdict line.
         exit 2
```

The reason is read from `err.code` **only when `err.status == null`** — a spawn failure sets `status` to
`null`, not `undefined`, so a guard written `=== undefined` does not fire, and `?? 1` then turns that `null`
into a 1 that reads like a reader which ran and found something. That is the third distinct JavaScript
subtlety behind one class, and the class is one sentence:

> **A process that never started and a process that ran and found nothing must not print the same line.**

Not decided here: the three tools that *do* state a FAIL at `rc 1` are not obviously the same event.
`falsify_comment_plane` reports 57 arms with 0 held, and whether every one of those is this environment or
some of them are real is a question this census asks and does not answer.
